content.title: Robert MacIntyre holds two-shot lead at Valero Texas Open as Round 3 suspended - PGA TOUR
content.text: 11D AGOVideo Player is loading.Current Time Duration Remaining Time captions settings, opens captions settings dialogcaptions off, selectedEnglishRobert MacIntyre's 81-yard approach sets up birdie on No. 5 at ValeroSAN ANTONIO — A long and soggy Sunday awaits the field at the Valero Texas Open.“We’re done,” PGA TOUR rules official Ken Tackett said. “The golf course just can’t take any more.”No players finished on Saturday. The final group of Robert MacIntyre (first/15 under), Ludvig Åberg (second/13 under) and Kevin Roy (T10/9 under) completed six holes, while players such as Matt Wallace and Marco Penge finished 14. Wallace, 11 under overall, was 7 under on his day when play was called, with two eagles on his card. Penge, who made seven birdies on his opening nine, was at 10 under.That’s when the horn blew, suspending play on TOUR for the fifth time this season.Light rain soon fell. Then it became sheets. Sheets became more sheets, in waves and waves and waves.“Unfortunately, the system stalled out on us,” Tackett said.Typically a springtime tournament, the 104-year-old Valero Texas Open often gets round-suspending showers – and, once many years ago, snow.Bad weather in San Antonio even played a role in TOUR history. During a delay in 1928, Tommy Armour and other players filled the time by formalizing bylaws for the Professional Touring Golfers’ Association, a forerunner of the PGA TOUR.
